strategy.name: Cautious Quality-Momentum, Low-Vol Tilt
strategy.rationale: Regime has been Cautious (score 2) for five months, so base equity is 65% with the remainder in cash. Selection: rank the 56-stock universe by blended 3m/12m momentum, then penalize annualized volatility. This avoids high-vol, deteriorating speculative names (RGTI, QUBT, LEU, SMR) and favors durable leaders across sectors (e.g. XOM, MRK, JNJ, NUE, AMD). 15 names limits single-name risk (~4.3% of NAV each at 65% invested). Monthly rebalance matches the cadence of the regime signal and keeps turnover moderate. Macro backdrop: oil at ~$108-115 (+22% in 90 days), 10Y at 5.0%, weak consumer confidence at 48, and sticky inflation. That argues against full equity exposure and for an energy/defensive tilt. Breadth is middling (50% above the 50d average), so I am not leaning on concentrated index beta. No planned_sell_date because the user gave no horizon.

rebalance_triggers.condition: Regime label changes (e.g. Cautious -> Defensive/Risk-Off, or -> Risk-On) at a monthly check
rebalance_triggers.action: Reset equity exposure to the equity_by_regime value and rebalance to top-N immediately

rebalance_triggers.condition: Brent/WTI rises >15% in 30 days or DGS10 closes above 5.25%
rebalance_triggers.action: Cut equity exposure by one regime step, favor low-vol names (vol<0.35) and energy/defensive holdings

rebalance_triggers.condition: Market breadth: pct_above_50d falls below 0.35 or QQQ 3-month momentum turns negative
rebalance_triggers.action: Move to Defensive allocation (40%) and trim names with vol>0.6 first

rebalance_triggers.condition: Single position drifts above 10% of NAV or an individual name falls more than 15% from entry
rebalance_triggers.action: Trim to target weight or exit; replace with next-ranked candidate

strategy.risk_notes: Long-only, with no guarantee of returns. Momentum can reverse sharply, e.g. CAT has a negative 3m return despite a strong 12m, and AMD/INTC are very high-vol. A 65% equity weight will probably lag QQQ in a strong rally. Oil shocks and 5% yields could compress valuations. Cash drag is the cost of the cautious stance. The stop-loss is evaluated against entry, so gaps can exceed 15%. The KR/US mix carries FX risk. The backtest window is short (2 years), so parameters are not heavily tuned and results are sensitive to regime-signal timing.

result.report_markdown:
## Verdict
**Underperformed, with worse risk-adjusted results.** Over the ~2-year window the strategy returned 27.9% against 44.1% for the benchmark. Sharpe was 0.60 vs 0.93, and max drawdown was -27.2% vs -22.8%. The defensive design did not deliver defensive outcomes.

## What drove results
The digest has no per-regime P&L, so this is inference, not attribution.
- **Cautious (the last 5 months):** 65% equity with 35% cash explains part of the lag. Beta was 0.71, and the market was positive (QQQ 3m +5.6%).
- **Risk-On (earlier history):** 95% equity should have tracked the benchmark more closely, so the gap likely comes mostly from stock selection and the sell rules, not from the cash drag alone.
- **Volatility did not fall:** annualized vol was 22.0% vs 21.9% for the benchmark despite a 0.71 beta. That points to high idiosyncratic risk from a concentrated 15-name book.

## Weaknesses
- **The vol penalty is too weak.** Momentum still pulls in AMD and INTC (vol 0.61–0.67), which undercuts the "low-vol tilt."
- **The 60% take-profit caps winners.** AMD's 12m return is +247%, so a cap like this cuts off the very momentum the strategy is trying to capture.
- **The stop-loss and max-holding rules interact poorly with monthly rebalancing.** They can force exits near lows (CAT's 3m return is -12%).
- **Cash earns nothing in the model.** With the 10Y near 5%, this is an avoidable drag.
- **Regime timing is a risk.** The regime signal stayed at score 2 for 5 months, so exposure was largely static.
- **The sample is short.** Two years is not enough to trust any of these parameters.

## Tweaks to test
1. **Hard-cap volatility and weight by inverse vol.** Exclude names with vol above ~0.45 and size positions inversely to vol. This should lower drawdown without relying on cash.
2. **Remove the take-profit** and use a trailing stop (e.g., 20–25% from peak) instead. Test raising Cautious equity to ~75%, since a 65% weight cost return without cutting drawdown.
3. **Hold the cash sleeve in T-bills or short Treasuries,** and widen to 20–25 names to reduce single-name risk.

Re-run each change separately, then out-of-sample, before adopting any of them.
